title: Ripples across the Chilean sky
caption: Star trails over Cerro Armazones, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: At first sight this picture could be ripples spreading from a stone dropped into a lake. In fact, the long bright stripes are star trails over Cerro Armazones, a peak 3046 metres above sea level in the central Atacama Desert, in the Chilean Andes. Every stripe traces one star's journey across the night.

The stars' motion is too slow for the naked eye to notice, but leaving a camera's shutter open reveals it. Exposures as short as 15 minutes are enough. The photographer combined many shorter exposures into the final picture, and a very wide-angle lens takes in the celestial pole on the right and the celestial equator just over the short tower.

The sheer number of trails shows how good the sky at Armazones is. The air is extremely clear and, thanks to the remote mountaintop, there is no light pollution. That is one reason the mountain was chosen as the future home of the European Extremely Large Telescope.

understand.summary: This landscape photograph was made by combining many shorter exposures taken with a very wide-angle lens at Cerro Armazones, in visible light. Other settings and colour processing are not published.
understand.eye: The eye sees stars as fixed points. Only long exposure time, here built up from many shorter exposures, turns their slow motion into these rippling trails.
